ambiguities: Brunch, Breakfast items: "French toast" is listed twice (once plain, once again later in the same list). I included it once. Confirm whether the second entry was meant to be a different dish (e.g. a specific variation) or is a duplicate.

Brunch, Breakfast items: "Eggs" is listed with no preparation. Confirm whether this means eggs any style, and whether it should say so on the site.
Brunch: "Extra: Chilled shellfish raw bar" — confirm whether this is a course, an add-on with separate pricing, or a note. No price or minimum was given.
Brunch: no per-course selection counts are given anywhere (only "Menu price per person will depend on total items selected"). Confirm whether guests pick freely from every section.

Tour of Spain, Mains: "Paella Valenciana ... (4-8 guests only)" — the guest-count restriction is currently kept inside the dish description. Confirm whether it should be displayed as a separate availability note.
Tour of Spain: "Gazpacho – Chilled tomato and vegetable soup," ends mid-sentence with a comma in the source, so the description may be truncated. Confirm the intended full text.
Tour of Spain, Starters: "Croquetas ... filled with choice of ham, chicken, cod, or mushrooms" requires a second choice from the guest. Confirm how that should be presented.
Tour of Spain: there is no overall pricing/selection line for this menu (unlike Italian feast and Spanish tapas). Confirm whether the standard pricing note should be added.

Wild game, First course: "Roasted Corn Chowder- Duck Confit" is followed on the next line by "Charred corn relish, smoked paprika, chive oil". I merged both into one description ("Duck Confit, charred corn relish, smoked paprika, chive oil"). Confirm whether "Duck Confit" belongs in the dish name instead.
Wild game, Mains and Desserts: dish names and garnish lines are on separate lines with no dash separator. I treated the second line as the description in every case. Confirm that reading.

Italian feast, Primi: "Tagliatelle al Funghi" and "Linguine alla vongole" — standard Italian would be "ai funghi" and "alle vongole". Left exactly as written since it may be intentional; confirm before publishing.
Italian feast, Dolce: three tiramisu variants are listed (date and pistachio, traditional, strawberry basil). Confirm all three should appear.
Italian feast: "Insalata" appears after "Secondi" in the source. Confirm the intended display order of courses.
Key west inspired, Starters: "citrus supreme" is likely the culinary term "suprême" (citrus segments). Left as written; confirm.

Several menus mix sentence case and lowercase dish names (e.g. "honey roasted pears...", "strawberry basil tiramisu"). I preserved the chef's casing exactly; confirm whether names should be normalized for the website.
Spanish tapas and Brunch have no per-course selection counts, unlike the other menus. Confirm whether minimums apply (e.g. a minimum number of tapas per guest).
